Playbook.name: Potential Denial of Service (DoS) Attack - SOC Playbook

Reference.title: MITRE ATT and CK - T1498 Network Denial of Service

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: NETSCOUT Arbor Edge Defense reported volumetric / flood events (SYN, ICMP, rate-based, malformed/invalid packets) that could deny a JCB internet-facing banking service. Triage question: is a source actively flooding a bank service and threatening its availability (a DoS), or is this a small blocked spike / background noise / an authorised load test?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: A denial-of-service against Internet Banking, mobile or web services is a direct availability and reputational impact - customers cannot transact and the outage is publicly visible. Confirming impact and whether AED mitigation is holding is the priority.

Assets.AssetType: JCB internet-facing banking services behind NETSCOUT AED (bank range 91.223.202.0/24 - Internet Banking, mobile, OWA and web properties, organised into AED protection groups such as "Corporate Online", "JCB Mobile ICS", "TEJARI WEBSITE")

LogSources.LogSource: NETSCOUT Arbor Edge Defense CEF - logs-cef.log-*

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: NETSCOUT AED CEF (verified live on JCB). Populated fields: source.ip, source.geo.country_name, source.as.organization.name, destination.ip, destination.port, network.transport, observer.product ("Arbor Edge Defense"), cef.device.event_class_id (flood/detection class), cef.extensions.deviceCustomString2 (protection group / bank service), cef.extensions.deviceCustomString6 (threat category, incl. "DDoS Botnets" / "DNS Flood"), cef.severity.

Relevant flood/volumetric detection classes observed live on JCB: "TCP SYN Flood Detection", "ICMP Flood Detection", "Rate-based Blocking", "TCP Connection Limiting", "TCP Connection Reset", "Invalid Packets", "Block Malformed DNS Traffic", "Malformed HTTP Filtering".

Signal.Name: Volumetric / Flood Events Against a Bank Service
Signal.Details: A surge of flood-class events against a protected bank service above the rule threshold.

Input.name: $srcip
Input.description: Source IP generating the flood the alert attributes the DoS to (source.ip - primary entity).

Input.name: $target
Input.description: Targeted bank asset under attack (destination.ip). Used to measure whether the flood is single-source (DoS) or distributed (DDoS).

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the full evidence story per the ClassificationGuidance - flood volume, class, whether AED blocked it, and how concentrated the sources are - not any single fact. If the load against the target comes from many distributed sources, treat it as a DDoS and use the DDoS playbook/response.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether a source is actively flooding a JCB service (scale, flood type, targeted asset), whether AED is mitigating it, and whether the attack is single-source (DoS) or distributed (DDoS).

Step.name: Flood volume and targets for the source
Step.Purpose: Characterise the alerting source: how much flood traffic, which flood classes and threat categories, against which bank services and ports.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE observer.vendor == "NETSCOUT" AND source.ip == "$srcip" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS events = COUNT(*), dst_ips = COUNT_DISTINCT(destination.ip), flood_classes = VALUES(cef.device.event_class_id), threat_cats = VALUES(cef.extensions.deviceCustomString6), services = VALUES(cef.extensions.deviceCustomString2), transports = VALUES(network.transport), ports = VALUES(destination.port), product = VALUES(observer.product) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: High event volume from one source against a bank service via a flood class (SYN/ICMP flood, rate-based blocking) = a single-source DoS. A handful of "Invalid Packets"/malformed events is often background noise. Note the flood_classes and whether they are volumetric (flood/rate) vs protocol hygiene (invalid/malformed).

Step.name: Source concentration on the targeted asset (DoS vs DDoS)
Step.Purpose: The decisive discriminator: whether the targeted asset is being hit by one/few sources (DoS) or many distributed sources (DDoS).
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE observer.vendor == "NETSCOUT" AND destination.ip == "$target" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS events = COUNT(*), src_countries = COUNT_DISTINCT(source.geo.country_name), asn = VALUES(source.as.organization.name) BY source.ip | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: One (or very few) source IPs dominating the events against the target = a DoS (this playbook). Many comparable sources across many countries = a distributed attack (DDoS) - switch to the DDoS playbook/response. Grounding: live JCB "DDoS Botnets" activity against a single bank IP has been seen from ~180 distinct sources across ~20 countries - that pattern is DDoS, not DoS.

Step.name: Flood classes and scale on the targeted service
Step.Purpose: The flood-class and volume breakdown on the targeted service shows the attack's nature and whether AED mitigation classes are engaging.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE observer.vendor == "NETSCOUT" AND destination.ip == "$target" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS events = COUNT(*), sources = COUNT_DISTINCT(source.ip), ports = VALUES(destination.port) BY cef.device.event_class_id, cef.extensions.deviceCustomString2 | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: Rate-based / SYN-flood / ICMP-flood / connection-limiting classes with high event counts indicate active volumetric mitigation by AED (mitigation engaging = good). Confirm the protected service (deviceCustomString2) is a real, in-use bank service and check its availability directly.

Node.Condition: Sustained volumetric flood (SYN/ICMP/rate-based) from one or a few sources against a real bank service, with AED mitigating and availability at risk.
Node.Result: True Positive (DoS Attack - engage DoS response, confirm mitigation and service availability)

Node.Condition: The targeted asset is being hit by many distributed sources across many countries (INV-02).
Node.Result: Needs Escalation / Reclassify as DDoS (use the DDoS playbook and response)

Node.Condition: A small or single-packet spike, background "Invalid Packets"/malformed noise fully blocked by AED, with no service impact - or an authorised load test.
Node.Result: False Positive (proven-blocked spike, or authorised load test)

Node.Condition: A real flood, but scale, source concentration or service impact cannot be established from available telemetry.

FalsePositive.Definition: An authorised or proven-blocked event - a scheduled load/performance test, or low-volume background flood/invalid-packet noise that AED blocked with no impact. Never classify simply as "benign".

Indicators.Item: Single or very few sources, low event volume, non-volumetric classes (e.g. isolated "Invalid Packets").
AED blocked every event; the targeted service stayed available.
The traffic maps to a known/scheduled load test or maintenance window.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm no availability impact and/or the authorised test; document; close as proven-blocked or authorised. Tune AED thresholds only with owner sign-off.

TruePositive.Definition: An active denial-of-service: a source (or few sources) generating volumetric flood traffic that threatens a bank service's availability.

Indicators.Item: High-volume flood-class events (SYN/ICMP/rate-based) concentrated from one/few sources against a real bank service.
Signs of AED mitigation engaging (rate-based blocking, connection limiting) and/or measurable service degradation.
Targeting of a live, customer-facing service (Internet Banking, mobile, OWA).

SOCAction.Item: Engage DoS response; confirm AED mitigation is holding and monitor service availability; block/rate-limit the source upstream; coordinate with the ISP/upstream scrubbing if impact persists.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the targeted service and whether it is degraded or down; check availability directly.
Establish single-source (DoS) vs distributed (DDoS) from INV-02 and route to the correct response.
Verify AED mitigation is engaging for the flood classes on the target (INV-03).

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Block/rate-limit the offending source(s) upstream; confirm AED mitigation is holding; coordinate with the ISP/upstream scrubbing provider if service impact continues; keep monitoring availability.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Tune AED protection thresholds for the affected service; validate upstream scrubbing capacity; document the attack (source, flood type, scale) for capacity planning and blocklisting.

Escalation.Trigger: Confirmed service degradation/outage, a distributed source pattern (reclassify as DDoS), or a real flood whose scale/impact cannot be established.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Proven-blocked spike or authorised load test confirmed; no availability impact; documented.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: DoS source blocked/rate-limited; AED mitigation confirmed; service availability restored and verified; attack documented for capacity planning.
